'''Luiz Vieira Caldas Saldanha''' (16 December 1937 – 16 November 1997) was a Portuguese [[marine biologist]], [[oceanographer]] and university professor at the [[University of Lisbon (1911–2013)#Faculty of Sciences|Faculty of Sciences, University of Lisbon]]. He was noted for research on [[marine fauna]] of the [[Atlantic Northeast]] and for his participation in international oceanographic campaigns and institutions, as well as for his role in developing and coordinating marine science and [[Marine technology|technology]] in [[Portugal]].<ref name="CIUHCT">{{cite web |url=https://dicionario.ciuhct.org/saldanha-luiz-vieira-caldas/ |title=Saldanha, Luiz Vieira Caldas |author1=Pedro Ré |author2=Armando J. Almeida |publisher=Centro Interuniversitário de História das Ciências e da Tecnologia (CIUHCT) |access-date=5 June 2023 |language=pt}}</ref><ref name="Re2001">{{cite web |url=https://webpages.ciencias.ulisboa.pt/~ajalmeida/Meus/42_Re_2001.pdf |title=Luiz Saldanha (1937–1997) – A paixão pelo mar |author1=Pedro Ré |author2=Armando J. Almeida |publisher=Faculdade de Ciências, Universidade de Lisboa |date=April 2001 |access-date=5 June 2023 |language=pt |format=PDF}}</ref>

Saldanha took part in oceanographic campaigns and expeditions across multiple ocean basins and regions worldwide, and worked for extended periods with research institutions in countries including [[France]], the [[United Kingdom]], the [[United States]] and [[Monaco]].<ref name="CIUHCT" /><ref name="Re2001" /> From 1969, he also conducted deep-sea research using crewed submersibles such as the French ''[[Archimède]]'' and ''[[Nautile]]'' and the American ''[[DSV Alvin|Alvin]]'', playing a decisive role in the discovery of the first [[hydrothermal vents and seamounts of the Azores]].<ref name="CIUHCT" /><ref name="Re2001" /><ref name="IC"/>

In [[Portugal]], Saldanha helped establish university-level teaching in several areas of [[marine biology]], including [[ichthyology]] and [[biological oceanography]], and trained numerous marine biologists who later became researchers and lecturers in Portugal and abroad.<ref name="CIUHCT" /><ref name="Re2001" /> He played a central role in strengthening marine-science infrastructure and coordination, notably through the revitalisation and direction of the [[Fort of Nossa Senhora da Guia (Cascais)|Guia Marine Laboratory]] in [[Cascais]] (1974–1997).<ref name="Re2001" /> He also held senior institutional posts, including president of the [[Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera|National Institute for Fisheries Research]] (INIP), and served in leadership roles within Portuguese and international scientific organisations.<ref name="CIUHCT" /><ref name="Re2001" />

== Biography ==

=== Early life and education ===
Saldanha was born on 16 December 1937 in Lisbon (São Sebastião da Pedreira). He attended the [[Lycée français Charles Lepierre]] in Lisbon, where he completed primary and secondary education. In those years he took part in a [[Scout group]] connected to the Church of Saint Louis of the Frenchmen (Lisbon), fostering an interest in nature exploration.<ref name="OMP">{{cite web |url=https://publications.cm-funchal.pt/jspui/bitstream/100/838/1/Bolmmf_s06_2001_ppi-viii.pdf |title=O meu Pai |author=Miguel Saldanha |publisher=Câmara Municipal do Funchal |access-date=17 May 2023 |language=pt |format=PDF}}</ref> He was a nephew of the archaeologist [[Eduardo da Cunha Serrão]] and accompanied him on excavations and other [[archaeological]] work from an early age, which contributed to his scientific curiosity.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.patrimoniocultural.gov.pt/static/data/publicacoes/o_arqueologo_portugues/serie_4/volume_1/estacao_parede.pdf |title=A estação pré-histórica de Parede |author=Eduardo da Cunha Serrão |publisher=Direção-Geral do Património Cultural |access-date=17 May 2023 |language=pt |format=PDF}}</ref> According to family testimony, his later interest in animal life and biology was primarily self-motivated.<ref name="OMP" />

=== Diving and early oceanographic work ===
As a young man, Saldanha became one of the pioneers of [[scuba diving]] in Portugal. In 1956, aged 18 and already a university student, he made his first dive off [[Sesimbra]] using borrowed equipment and without a wetsuit. A few months later, invited by [[Mário Ruivo]] of the ''Instituto de Biologia Marinha'' (Institute of Marine Biology), he joined his first oceanographic campaign aboard the naval vessel ''Faial'', where he met visiting foreign researchers and began corresponding with them.<ref name="OMP" />

=== Academic career, military service and museums ===
In 1961, Saldanha graduated in [[Biological Sciences]] from the Faculty of Sciences ([[University of Lisbon]]), completing his final courses while performing extended military service as an army officer. In 1962, already married, he was posted to [[Angola]] during the [[Portuguese Colonial War]] and remained there for two years and three months (1962–1965), in the Northern Intervention Zone (ZIN).<ref name="CIUHCT" /> Alongside military duties, he carried out scientific collecting and improved his [[taxidermy]] techniques, later depositing specimens at the ''Museu Bocage'' (now part of the [[National Museum of Natural History and Science, Lisbon]]).<ref name="Re2001" />

After completing military service in 1965, he began his professional career (aged 27) as a naturalist at the ''Museu Bocage''. He remained there until 1970, when he moved to the Zoological and Anthropological Museum and Laboratory of the Faculty of Sciences as a researcher.<ref name="CIUHCT" />

In 1974 he completed a PhD in Sciences ([[Animal Ecology]]) at the Faculty of Sciences, graduating with distinction, and began a long teaching career at the same faculty: assistant professor (1975), extraordinary professor (1978) and full professor (1979).<ref name="CIUHCT" /><ref name="Re2001" />

=== Guia Marine Laboratory ===
In 1974, the same year he earned his doctorate, Saldanha led the recovery of the [[Fort of Nossa Senhora da Guia (Cascais)|Fort of Nossa Senhora da Guia]] in [[Cascais]], where he reactivated and developed the Guia Marine Laboratory (Portuguese: ''Laboratório Marítimo da Guia'').<ref name="ULisboaGuia">{{cite web |url=https://www.ulisboa.pt/patrimonio/laboratorio-maritimo-da-guia-forte-de-nossa-senhora-da-guia |title=Laboratório Marítimo da Guia / Forte de Nossa Senhora da Guia |publisher=Universidade de Lisboa |access-date=30 June 2020 |language=pt}}</ref> He requested the fort's classification as a Property of Public Interest in April 1974, approved in 1977, and supervised research and undergraduate field projects there in [[marine biology]] and [[biological oceanography]]. He directed the laboratory from 1974 until his death in 1997.<ref name="Re2001" />

=== Research and science communication ===
Saldanha's research and oceanographic campaigns were not limited to Portuguese waters. He worked for extended periods in laboratories in France, the United Kingdom, the United States and Monaco, and participated in expeditions in the [[Mediterranean Sea]], the [[Atlantic Ocean]], the [[Arctic Ocean]], the [[Indian Ocean]], the [[Pacific Ocean]] and [[Antarctica]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cvc.instituto-camoes.pt/ciencia/p14.html |title=Luiz Vieira Caldas Saldanha (1937–1997) |author=Fernando Reis |publisher=Ciência em Portugal (Instituto Camões) |access-date=30 June 2020 |language=pt}}</ref> The breadth of these voyages led some Portuguese media to refer to him as the “man of the seven seas”.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Luiz Saldanha, o homem dos Sete Mares |author=João Paulo Sacadura |magazine=Fórum Ambiente |date=1994 |issue=8 |pages=13–15 |language=pt}}</ref>

From 1969, he regularly dived using the French submersibles ''[[Archimède]]'' and ''[[Nautile]]'' and the American ''[[DSV Alvin|Alvin]]'' to study [[deep-sea]] biology and hydrothermal fauna.<ref name="CIUHCT" /><ref name="Re2001" /> In 1992, aboard ''Alvin'', he was responsible for identifying the first of the [[hydrothermal vents and seamounts of the Azores]], the Lucky Strike hydrothermal field.<ref name="IC"/>

Beyond marine work, he also carried out terrestrial expeditions in desert regions, often travelling with traditional caravans, and paid attention to the human and [[ethnographic]] aspects of the communities he encountered.<ref name="CIUHCT" />

In March 1978, a fire at the Faculty of Sciences building (then at the former Lisbon Polytechnic School) destroyed Saldanha's laboratory and much of his equipment, manuscripts, notes, books and reprints, as well as most of the zoological collection he had assembled in Angola, causing significant delays to ongoing scientific work.<ref name="CIUHCT" />

Saldanha placed strong emphasis on science communication. He delivered numerous lectures in Portugal and abroad, served on editorial and review boards of scientific journals, and authored documentary series for [[Rádio e Televisão de Portugal|RTP]], the Portuguese [[public service broadcaster]], including ''Missão Açores'' (1984)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://arquivos.rtp.pt/programas/missao-acores/ |title=Missão Açores |publisher=RTP Arquivos |access-date=5 June 2023 |language=pt}}</ref> and ''O Mar e a Terra'' (1985, 1987).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://arquivos.rtp.pt/programas/o-mar-e-a-terra/ |title=O Mar e a Terra |publisher=RTP Arquivos |access-date=5 June 2023 |language=pt}}</ref>

=== Nature conservation ===
[[File:Serra da Arrábida - Praia nascente e Península de Tróia.jpg|thumb|View from the [[Serra da Arrábida]] over the waters later included in the Professor Luiz Saldanha Marine Park.]]
Committed to nature conservation from early on, in 1965 Saldanha and colleagues from the Portuguese Centre for Underwater Activities (CPAS) submitted a proposal to the [[Navy Ministry (Portugal)|Navy Ministry]] calling for a [[marine reserve]] along the coast of the [[Serra da Arrábida]]. Although the proposal was not adopted at the time, 33 years later, in 1998, the area proposed by Saldanha was designated the [[Professor Luiz Saldanha Marine Park]], within the [[Arrábida Natural Park]].<ref name="CIUHCT" /><ref name="UAlg">{{cite web |url=https://arrabidaparquemarinho.ualg.pt/ |title=Parque Marinho Professor Luiz Saldanha |publisher=Universidade do Algarve |access-date=5 June 2023 |language=pt}}</ref><ref name="NG">{{cite web |url=https://nationalgeographic.sapo.pt/natureza/grandes-reportagens/2481-nas-aguas-da-arrabida |title=Nas águas do Parque Marinho Professor Luiz Saldanha na Arrábida |author=Hugo Marques |publisher=National Geographic Portugal |date=July 2020 |access-date=29 July 2020 |language=pt}}</ref>

He collaborated with organisations dedicated to conservation, notably the ''[[Liga para a Protecção da Natureza]]'' (LPN), serving as president of its board (1985–1987) and later president of its general assembly.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lpn.pt/pt/noticias/inauguracao-da-exposicao-arrabida-um-laboratorio-natural-para-o-estudo-do-oceano/ |title=Inauguração da exposição “Arrábida: um laboratório natural para o estudo do oceano” |publisher=Liga para a Protecção da Natureza |date=7 June 2021 |access-date=9 June 2023 |language=pt}}</ref><ref name="CIUHCT" />

=== Institutional leadership roles ===
Saldanha held several institutional leadership positions nationally and internationally. In 1987 he became president of the National Institute for Fisheries Research (INIP), an organisation later integrated into the ''[[Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera]]'' (IPMA).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://arquivos.rtp.pt/conteudos/posse-da-nova-direccao-do-inip/ |title=Posse da nova direcção do INIP |publisher=RTP Arquivos |date=2 January 1987 |access-date=30 June 2020 |language=pt}}</ref><ref name="Re2001" /> As noted above, he was also president of LPN's board (1985–1987) and later president of its general assembly.<ref name="CIUHCT" /><ref name="Re2001" />

He served as vice-president of the [[International Council for the Exploration of the Sea]] (ICES), as a delegate in European marine science programmes, and as a member of scientific bodies connected to the ''[[Institut océanographique]]'' of Monaco and the [[Oceanographic Museum]]. He also worked with international scientific academies and European science organisations.<ref name="Re2001" />

In 1991 he promoted the creation of the ''Instituto do Mar'' (IMAR), with the aim of gathering marine-science researchers in Portugal, and served as its first president of the board and scientific council.<ref name="Re2001" />

=== Artistic interests ===
Saldanha maintained a notable artistic practice alongside his scientific career. During expeditions he kept illustrated diaries with [[watercolours]] and [[coloured pencil]] drawings depicting landscapes, observed species and notable moments, some of which were later exhibited and published.<ref name="CIUHCT" />

He also collected and crafted [[Scale model|miniature lead soldiers]], [[Model building|creating]] and painting historically themed [[dioramas]]; the quality of this work earned awards at specialist exhibitions.<ref name="Re2001" />

=== Death ===
Saldanha died on 16 November 1997 at his residence in [[Cascais]] after a prolonged illness. His death occurred on Portugal's National Sea Day, a date associated with public recognition of the oceans to which he dedicated his career.<ref name="PFTS">{{cite journal |last1=Ré |first1=Pedro |last2=Almeida |first2=Armando J. |last3=Biscoito |first3=Manuel |title=Luiz Vieira Caldas Saldanha: Passion for the Sea |journal=Boletim do Museu Municipal do Funchal |series=Supplement |issue=6 |date=2001 |pages=5–13 |url=http://lmg.fc.ul.pt/luizsaldanha.pdf |access-date=21 December 2012 |language=en}}</ref>

== Honours and tributes ==

=== Honours received during his lifetime ===
During his lifetime, Saldanha received multiple honours, particularly from international organisations. Notable distinctions include:
* [[Albert I, Prince of Monaco#The Great Albert I Medals|Grande Médaille Albert Ier]] (Monaco): awarded in 1988 by the ''[[Institut océanographique]]'' of Monaco in recognition of his contributions to marine science.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.oceano.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/GMAI_liste_mai21.pdf |title=Les Grandes Médailles Albert Ier |publisher=Institut océanographique, Fondation Albert Ier, Prince de Monaco |access-date=5 June 2023 |language=fr |format=PDF}}</ref>
* Officer of the [[Order of Grimaldi]] (Monaco): awarded by Prince [[Rainier III of Monaco]].<ref name="Re2001" />
* Commander of the ''[[Ordre des Palmes Académiques]]'' (France), for teaching and scientific outreach.<ref name="Re2001" />
* Manley Bendall "Maritime Personality of the Year Award" (France), awarded by the ''[[Académie de marine]]''.<ref name="Re2001" />
* ''[[Tridente d'Oro]]'' (Italy), awarded in 1990 by the International Academy of Underwater Sciences and Techniques (Italian: ''Accademia Internazionale di Scienze e Tecniche Subacquee'').<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.underwateracademy.org/tridenti-1990-99/ |title=Tridenti 1990–99 |publisher=Accademia Internazionale di Scienze e Tecniche Subacquee |access-date=5 June 2023}}</ref>

=== Posthumous tributes ===
After his death, Saldanha was widely honoured for his legacy. Major tributes include:
* [[Professor Luiz Saldanha Marine Park]]: created in 1998 and named in his honour as the first marine reserve on mainland Portugal, integrated in the [[Arrábida Natural Park]].<ref name="UAlg" /><ref name="NG" />
* Luiz Saldanha Oceanographic Museum ([[Setúbal]] area): the oceanographic museum at [[Fort Santa Maria da Arrábida]] bears his name.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://biomares.ccmar.ualg.pt/historia_museu.html |title=A História do Museu |publisher=CCMAR/BIOMARES |access-date=1 July 2020 |language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.azeitao.net/arrabida/pna/museu.html |title=Museu Oceanográfico |publisher=Azeitão.net |access-date=1 July 2020 |language=pt}}</ref>
* Saldanha Hydrothermal Field and "Missão Saldanha": in 1998 an expedition led by Fernando Barriga discovered a seamount and hydrothermal vent system in the Azores region, named in his honour.<ref name="IC">{{cite web |url=http://cvc.instituto-camoes.pt/ciencia/e12.html |title=A Missão Saldanha |author=Nuno Crato |publisher=Ciência em Portugal (Instituto Camões) |date=2003 |access-date=19 December 2012 |language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.oceanario.pt/cms/1266 |title=Monte Saldanha |author=Nuno Crato |publisher=Oceanário de Lisboa |access-date=20 December 2012 |language=pt}}</ref>
* [[Lisbon Oceanarium]]: in 1998 a venue space was named “Sala Professor Luiz Saldanha”; after the Oceanarium concession changed in 2016, it was renamed “Sala [[Sophia de Mello Breyner Andresen|Sophia de Mello Breyner]]”.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://informacoeseservicos.lisboa.pt/contactos/diretorio-da-cidade/oceanario-espacos-para-eventos |title=Oceanário – Espaços para Eventos |publisher=Câmara Municipal de Lisboa |access-date=30 June 2020 |language=pt}}</ref>
* Professor Luiz Saldanha Library: in 1999 the [[Funchal]] City Council created a specialised library with his scientific collection at the Funchal Marine Biology Station, later enriched with Armando J. Almeida's collection (2011).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cm-funchal.pt/pt/serviços/ciência/centro-de-informação-e-documentação/biblioteca-professor-luiz-saldanha |title=Biblioteca Professor Luiz Saldanha |publisher=Câmara Municipal do Funchal |access-date=30 June 2020 |language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://webpages.ciencias.ulisboa.pt/~ajalmeida/Fotos/Funchal_Outubro_2011/Espolio_EBMF.pdf |title=Biblioteca Professor Luiz Saldanha recebe novo espólio |publisher=Câmara Municipal do Funchal |date=23 November 2011 |access-date=5 June 2023 |language=pt |format=PDF}}</ref>
* Grand Officer of the [[Order of Saint James of the Sword]]: awarded posthumously on 28 October 1999 by President [[Jorge Sampaio]].<ref name="PFTS" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ordens.presidencia.pt/?idc=153 |title=Cidadãos Nacionais Agraciados com Ordens Portuguesas (search results) |publisher=Presidência da República Portuguesa |access-date=16 June 2014 |language=pt}}</ref>
* [[CTT Correios de Portugal|CTT Post of Portugal]]: on 16 November 1999, a commemorative “Sea Day” postcard was issued with his image.<ref name="Re2001" />
* [[Lisbon Geographic Society]]: on the same date, the society opened the exhibition ''Luiz Saldanha: Naturalista do Século XX'' at its museum.<ref name="Re2001" />
* [[National Museum of Natural History and Science, Lisbon|National Museum of Natural History and Science]] and the Guia Marine Laboratory: in December 2007 these institutions held a session marking the tenth anniversary of his death, and launched the book ''Luiz Saldanha e o Laboratório Marítimo da Guia'' (Armando J. Almeida and Pilar Pereira).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://triplov.com/biblos/Museu-Bocage/Factos-importantes.htm |title=Museu Bocage – datas e factos importantes |author=Maria João Ferreira |publisher=TriploV |access-date=5 June 2023 |language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/236619664_Luiz_Saldanha_e_o_Laboratorio_Maritimo_da_Guia_1975-1977_Ensino_e_Investigacao |title=Luiz Saldanha e o Laboratório Marítimo da Guia (1975–1977). Ensino e Investigação |author=Armando J. Almeida |publisher=Museu Nacional de História Natural |date=2007 |access-date=5 June 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.publico.pt/2008/03/02/jornal/em-estreia-251525 |title=Em estreia |newspaper=Público |date=2 March 2008 |access-date=5 June 2023 |language=pt}}</ref>

==== Recent tributes ====
* [[Funchal]] municipality: on 16 November 2021, Funchal again marked the anniversary of his death as part of Sea Day commemorations, with an evocative session at the [[Estação de Biologia Marinha do Funchal|Funchal Marine Biology Station]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.funchal.pt/camara-municipal-do-funchal-assinala-dia-mundial-do-mar-e-aniversario-da-morte-de-luiz-saldanha/ |title=Câmara Municipal do Funchal assinala Dia Mundial do Mar e aniversário da morte de Luiz Saldanha |publisher=Câmara Municipal do Funchal |date=17 November 2021 |access-date=5 June 2023 |language=pt}}</ref>
* [[Sesimbra]] municipality: on 7 May 2022 he was posthumously awarded the "Medalhão da Vila de Sesimbra" for his role in identifying and helping protect [[dinosaur track]] sites at [[Cape Espichel]] (Pedra da Mua, Lagosteiros and Pedreira do Avelino).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sesimbra.pt/noticia-72/sesimbra-distingue-luiz-saldanha-miguel-telles-e-galopim-de-carvalho |title=Sesimbra distingue Luiz Saldanha, Miguel Telles e Galopim de Carvalho |publisher=Câmara Municipal de Sesimbra |date=7 May 2022 |access-date=5 June 2023 |language=pt}}</ref>
* [[Vasco da Gama Aquarium]]: on 6 June 2023, he was honoured at the launch of the book ''Missão Oceanográfica Arquipélago da Madeira 1984'', which reproduces drawings and watercolours from his diary and underwater photography from Jorge Albuquerque, also honoured at the event.<ref name="Re2001" />

==== Toponymy ====
Saldanha's name has been used in local toponymy, including a street in [[Cascais]] (''Bairro do Rosário'') and a street in [[Tavira]] (Santa Luzia parish).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ruas.openalfa.pt/ruas/rua-luis-saldanha-alameda-da-guia-cascais-e-estoril-cascais |title=Rua Luis Saldanha, Cascais |publisher=Ruas de Portugal (OpenAlfa) |access-date=6 June 2023 |language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://ruas.openalfa.pt/ruas/rua-professor-luiz-saldanha-santa-luzia-freguesia-de-santa-luzia-concelho-de-tavira |title=Rua Professor Luiz Saldanha, Tavira |publisher=Ruas de Portugal (OpenAlfa) |access-date=6 June 2023 |language=pt}}</ref>

=== Taxa named after Saldanha ===
Saldanha has also been honoured in biological nomenclature, with species and subspecies named after him:
* ''[[Charaxes lucretius|Charaxes lucretius saldanhai]]'' (Bivar de Sousa, 1983) – Angolan butterfly subspecies.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://species.wikimedia.org/wiki/Charaxes_lucretius_saldanhai |title=Charaxes lucretius saldanhai |publisher=Wikispecies |access-date=5 June 2023}}</ref>
* ''[[Coloconger saldanhai]]'' (Quéro, 2001) – species of eel in genus ''Coloconger''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fishwise.co.za/Default.aspx?TabID=110&SpecieConfigId=290056 |title=Coloconger saldanhai |publisher=Fishwise |access-date=25 September 2013 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131215142605/http://www.fishwise.co.za/Default.aspx?TabID=110&SpecieConfigId=290056 |archive-date=2013-12-15}}</ref>
* ''[[Geocharis (beetle)|Geocharis saldanhai]]'' (A. Serrano & Aguiar, 2001) – beetle species.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://naturdata.com/Geocharis-saldanhai-35480.htm |title=Geocharis saldanhai |publisher=Naturdata |access-date=5 June 2023}}</ref>
* ''[[Ilyophis saldanhai]]'' (Karmovskaya & Parin, 1999) – eel species.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://eol.org/pages/208260 |title=Ilyophis saldanhai |publisher=Encyclopedia of Life |access-date=5 June 2023}}</ref>
* ''[[Ophidion (fish)|Ophidion saldanhai]]'' (Matallanas & Brito, 1999) – fish species recorded from Cabo Verde and the Gulf of Guinea region.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fishbase.se/summary/56309 |title=Ophidion saldanhai |publisher=FishBase |access-date=5 June 2023}}</ref>
* ''[[Pachycara|Pachycara saldanhai]]'' (Biscoito & Almeida, 2004) – deep-sea fish species.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fishbase.se/summary/62054 |title=Pachycara saldanhai |publisher=FishBase |access-date=5 June 2023}}</ref>
* ''Puellina saldanhai'' (Harmelin, 2001) – microscopic marine animal recorded from southern Portugal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.marinespecies.org/aphia.php?p=taxdetails&id=221546 |title=Puellina saldanhai |publisher=World Register of Marine Species |access-date=5 June 2023}}</ref>

== Selected works ==
Saldanha published around 130 scientific works in Portuguese and international journals, and five books. Due to the long list of publications, only a selection is provided here.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.triplov.com/biblos/saldanha.htm |title=Luiz Saldanha |publisher=TriploV |access-date=5 June 2023 |language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://lmg.fc.ul.pt/biblio_saldanha.pdf |title=List of publications of Luiz Saldanha from 1959 up to 2001 |author=Armando J. Almeida |publisher=Faculdade de Ciências de Lisboa |access-date=5 June 2023 |language=en |format=PDF}}</ref>

* 1959 – ''Como nasceu a secção de estudos submarinos da Sociedade Portuguesa de Ciências Naturais''. ''Naturália'', 8(1): 1–5.
* 1960 – ''Recordando a Zoologia''. ''CPAS. Revista Portuguesa de Actividades Subaquáticas'', 2: 1–2.
* 1962 – ''Exploração submarina''. ''O Sesimbrense'', 359: 1, 3.
* 1965 – ''Sobre três espécies de teleósteos (Nettastomidae e Notacanthidae) novas para a Costa de Portugal''. ''Notas e Estudos do Instituto de Biologia Marinha'', 32/3: 1–18.
* 1965 – ''As espécies cinegéticas do Norte de Angola''. ''Caça e tiro ao voo'', 7: 32–33, 36.

* 1967 – ''Vasos cerâmicos de Angola''. ''Geographica'', Year III, no. 10: 35–56.
* 1968 – ''Noroeste de Angola''. ''Geographica'', Year IV, no. 13: 71–85.
* 1971 – ''Observations bionomiques à “Pedra da Anixa”''. ''Bulletin de l’Association des professeurs de Biologie–Géologie'', Suppl. 201: 127–132.
* 1973 – ''La côte du Mozambique. Résultats d’une exploration zoologique préliminaire''. ''Bulletin du Muséum national d’Histoire naturelle'' (Paris), (3), 158, Écologie générale, 14: 249–259.
* 1974 – ''Estudo do povoamento dos horizontes da rocha litoral da costa da Arrábida''. Museu Bocage (PhD thesis).
* 1974 – ''Sobre a forma das grandes profundidades marinhas e sua origem''. Museu Bocage (doctoral complementary examination).
* 1980 – ''Fauna Submarina Atlântica''. Publicações Europa-América.
* 1980 – ''Estudo ambiental do estuário do Tejo: povoamentos bentónicos, peixes e ictioplancton do estuário do Tejo''. Comissão Nacional do Ambiente/Tejo, no. 5 – Report 4.
* 1982 – ''O rei D. Carlos pioneiro da Oceanografia europeia''. ''Revista de Marinha'', no. 110: 3–8.
* 1986 – ''A protecção e a conservação do meio marinho''. In ''Que futuro para a costa Sudoeste'' (Ambiente em discussão 1), pp.&nbsp;51–55. Liga para a Protecção da Natureza.
* 1988 – ''A protecção e a conservação do meio marinho nos Açores e na Madeira''. ''Primeiras Jornadas Atlânticas de Protecção do Meio Ambiente'', pp.&nbsp;315–317. Angra do Heroísmo.
* 1989 – ''Euskal Herriko itsas sakonetaro fauna'' (''Fauna marinha profunda do País Basco''). Krisaly, 101 pp.
* 1992 – ''Um parque marinho no Espichel''. ''Sesimbra cultural'', 2: 41–43.
* 1993 – ''Prince Albert of Monaco and King Carlos of Portugal: Their contribution to the knowledge of the Atlantic deep-sea fauna''. Abstracts of the V International Congress on the History of Oceanography, 1 p.
* 1994 – ''Germano da Fonseca Sacarrão – Um Biólogo Marinho, um Grande Amigo''. In ''Professor Germano da Fonseca Sacarrão (1914–1992)''. Museu Bocage, pp.&nbsp;73–86.
* 1995 – ''Fauna submarina Atlântica: Portugal continental, Açores, Madeira'' (2nd ed., revised and expanded). Publicações Europa-América.
* 1997 – ''One hundred years of Portuguese Oceanography in the footsteps of King Carlos Bragança''. Museu Bocage.
